Elena / team —

Attaching the first-draft mapping (redwood-export-controls-mapping.xlsx). High-level notes in the spreadsheet and summarized below:

Summary:
- Storage regions: Customer data for Lumina Health can be pinned to us-east-1 (US), eu-west-1 (IE), or ap-south-1 (IN) depending on the deployment option. By default hosted customers are in a regional partition; we include region metadata in every object.
- Cross-border transfers: For hosted customers using eu regions, transitory processing can occur in the US for model inference (if you choose the multi-region inference routing option). Our default for regulated customers is to configure routing to keep inference and storage within EU only.
- Transfer mechanisms: We support EU adequacy (where applicable), SCCs (we provide an Annex and execution template), and customer-managed keys for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) scenarios. For customers requiring explicit DPF mapping we provide an Annex + a transfer risk log.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest (KMS-managed keys). TLS 1.3 in transit. We also document per-customer KMS keys and rotation cadence in the policy. See s3-encryption-policy.txt for the KMS key policy excerpt.
- Subprocessors: Attached list is a 90-day snapshot in the spreadsheet (row / sheet labeled "subprocessors"). We notify customers per contract when we add a subprocessors that will handle customer data.

Open items we will add to the final bundle:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — available on request via secure link to your audit team.
- DPA Annex + SCC execution package (we can pre-fill Lumina's legal name if you confirm).
- A one-page attestation for the DPF package if you want signatures.

Attachments included: redwood-export-controls-mapping.xlsx (spreadsheet), s3-encryption-policy.txt (policy excerpt). Final evidence PDF (dpft-evidence-pack.pdf) will follow once Monica compiles screenshots for key rotation and KMS console views.

Let me know if you'd like a short call to walk the sheet (I can do 11–12 PST tomorrow).

Thanks,
Neha
